machine_state_during_measurement.why_it_matters: A scaling curve measured against a contended machine is an artifact of the contention. This table was deliberately held back until the machine was idle.
machine_state_during_measurement.run_order: DESCENDING (16, 8, 4, 2, 1), so the most oversubscription-sensitive point ran first on the demonstrably cleanest machine.
machine_state_during_measurement.contiguity_evidence: Runs are sequential and non-overlapping: 04:20:41->04:29:14, 04:29:26->04:37:32, 04:37:43->04:47:47, 04:47:56->05:02:30, 05:02:43->05:26:05 UTC. No gaps, no overlap, single clean pass.

DEVIATION_DISCLOSED.what: The mandate specified a 120-motif scaling workload; this table uses 16 motifs.
DEVIATION_DISCLOSED.why: Measured per-motif cost makes a 1-worker 120-motif run roughly eight hours and the full table about fifteen, more than the speedup it exists to inform. The 16-motif table took 65 minutes.
DEVIATION_DISCLOSED.cost: Granularity at the top of the curve. 16 motifs on 16 workers is a single wave and on 8 workers only two, so pipeline-fill effects at the tail are proportionally larger than they would be in a production shard.
DEVIATION_DISCLOSED.BINDING_RULE: Any receipt citing the recommended worker count MUST state that it was read off a 16-motif curve. This claim is not to be silently upgraded.

DIGEST_EQUALITY_GATE.note: These are the SAME digests produced by the seeded storage runs on both D: and C:. The outputs are therefore invariant to worker count, storage location and machine contention. Rankings are included in the gate, which is only meaningful because the seed is pinned; before that fix a rankings difference would have been a seed artifact rather than a finding.

SATURATION_RESULT.basis: Measured wall-clock minimum. The curve is bracketed on both sides: 4 workers is 604 s, 8 workers is 486 s, 16 workers is 513 s.

mechanism_identified_not_merely_observed.scoring_phase: Keeps improving with workers but with sharp diminishing returns: 1131.5 -> 601.1 -> 339.6 -> 222.4 -> 184.0 s. Scoring speedup vs 1 worker is 1.88x, 3.33x, 5.09x, 6.15x, i.e. scoring-only efficiency falls from 0.94 to 0.38. Hyperthreading gives a real but partial benefit beyond the 8 physical cores.
mechanism_identified_not_merely_observed.non_scoring_phase: FLAT at 264-273 s for 1, 2, 4 and 8 workers, then jumps to 329 s at 16. It gains nothing from additional workers and is actively penalised once workers exceed physical cores.
mechanism_identified_not_merely_observed.net: The +65 s non-scoring penalty at 16 workers exceeds the 38 s scoring gain, so 16 is a net loss.
mechanism_identified_not_merely_observed.why_this_generalises: The penalty is a property of running more workers than physical cores, not of this particular workload size, so the same penalty is expected per shard in the full build.

bottleneck_classification.dominant: A large SERIAL component in the non-scoring phase.
bottleneck_classification.basis: non-scoring is ~265 s and does not fall with workers; 265/1402 = 0.189 of the 1-worker wall clock.
bottleneck_classification.interpretation: Overall parallel efficiency is poor (0.36 at the optimum) NOT because scoring parallelises badly -- it reaches 5.09x on 8 cores -- but because a ~265 s serial segment is paid regardless. This is the single most important fact for shard sizing: that segment is paid ONCE PER SHARD.
bottleneck_classification.not_CPU_bound_overall: The scoring phase is CPU-bound and parallel; the non-scoring phase is serial and is what caps the achievable speedup.

CONSEQUENCE_FOR_SHARD_SIZING.the_arithmetic: Each shard pays ~265 s of serial non-scoring cost. With N shards that is N x 265 s of pure overhead: 81 shards of 128 motifs would spend ~6.0 h on overhead alone, 21 shards of 512 motifs ~1.5 h, 10 shards of 1024 motifs ~0.7 h.
CONSEQUENCE_FOR_SHARD_SIZING.why_a_recommendation_is_NOT_made_here: Two things are unmeasured. (1) Whether the ~265 s is genuinely fixed or contains a write component proportional to motif count -- at 16 motifs the feathers are ~40 MB, at 512 they would be ~1.3 GB and writes could dominate. (2) Whether per-motif scoring cost improves with more motifs per run: at 8 workers a 16-motif run is only two waves, so tail effects are proportionally large and the measured 13.9 s/motif is likely pessimistic.
CONSEQUENCE_FOR_SHARD_SIZING.outstanding_measurement: A 128-motif run at 8 workers, using a motif list whose first 16 entries are exactly the bench16 list (verified nested), so the two points differ only in scale. This separates the fixed load from the per-motif write cost and tests whether per-motif scoring cost falls with better pipeline fill.
CONSEQUENCE_FOR_SHARD_SIZING.naive_projection_explicitly_withheld: 13.9 s/motif x 10,249 motifs = 39.6 h of scoring at 8 workers. This is NOT reported as the expected runtime, because it extrapolates a per-motif cost measured on a two-wave workload and would almost certainly overstate it.

concurrency_note.question: Can Route A and Route B build concurrently?
concurrency_note.answer_so_far: Running two builds at 8 workers each means 16 workers total, which this table shows is past saturation on 8 physical cores. Concurrency at 8+8 is therefore expected to be SLOWER than the same work run sequentially at 8. Not yet measured directly.
concurrency_note.additional_consideration: The union-score reuse proven in V69_UNION_REGION_SCORE_EQUIVALENCE_V1 means the expensive scoring pass should be run ONCE over the union of both region universes, which largely removes the need for route concurrency in the scoring phase.
